quandoUsar: Summary of indicators at the top of a dashboard: a number with a label, comparison context, and change.
Numbers that change with a filter or period: the digits roll to the new value and the texts enter from the side the number moved toward.
quandoEvitar: Use `animated-counter` when the animated number alone is enough, with no card, label, or context.
Use `stats-band` for highlight numbers on a marketing page.
Use `gauge` or `usage-meter` when the value only makes sense against a range or a limit.
acessibilidade: The animated number is `aria-hidden` and the final formatted value goes in a hidden text, so the screen reader reads the correct number in one go.
The card is an `<article>` with no heading of its own (the label is plain text): give the section that groups the cards a heading if the page needs that structure.
The change is colored by sign, but the `+` or `-` itself in the text already conveys the direction, without relying on color alone.
movimento: The digits roll from zero the first time the number enters the viewport; after that, each column rolls in the direction the value changed.
When `label`, `context`, or `change` change, the new text enters from below if its number rose or from above if it fell, and the change pill adjusts its width on a spring.
With “reduced motion”, the digits jump to the value and the texts swap with a quick fade.
responsivo: The card takes the parent's width; on screens up to 380 px the inner padding shrinks and the change pill may move to the line below.
notasIA: `value` is numeric and appears as an integer with a thousands separator in the `en-US` format: the card doesn't forward `decimals`, `prefix`, or `locale` to the counter, so put the currency in `label` and the unit in `suffix`.
`label`, `value`, and `context` are required; `change` is free text: if it starts with `+` it turns green and with `-` red, with no way to invert for metrics where a drop is good.
It needs the `animated-counter` item installed (the card imports it from `../animated-counter/animated-counter`); for a row of indicators, put the cards in a grid, since each one fills its own cell.
